subject: Maths
topic: Surface Areas and Volumes — Combined Solids

questions.q: A medicine capsule consists of a cylinder of diameter 0.5 cm with a hemisphere at each end. Its total length is 2 cm. Approximately what is its capacity using pi = 22/7?
questions.explanation: The radius is 0.25 cm, and the cylindrical part has height 2 - 0.5 = 1.5 cm. The two hemispheres together make one sphere, so volume = pi r^2 h + (4/3)pi r^3. Substitution gives approximately 0.36 cm^3.

questions.q: A metallic spherical shell has internal diameter 4 cm and external diameter 8 cm. It is melted into a cone of base diameter 8 cm. What is the cone height?
questions.explanation: The shell volume is (4/3)pi(4^3 - 2^3) = (224/3)pi cm^3. The cone has radius 4 cm, so its volume is (1/3)pi(4^2)h = (16/3)pi h. Equating volumes gives 16h = 224, so h = 14 cm.

questions.q: Two identical cubes, each of volume 64 cm^3, are joined face-to-face. What is the total surface area of the resulting cuboid?
questions.explanation: A cube of volume 64 cm^3 has side 4 cm. Joining two face-to-face forms a cuboid of dimensions 8 cm x 4 cm x 4 cm. Its total surface area is 2(8x4 + 4x4 + 8x4) = 160 cm^2.

questions.q: A solid toy is a hemisphere of radius 4 cm surmounted by a cone of the same radius and height 4 cm. What is its exposed total surface area?
questions.explanation: The joined circular base is internal, so only the curved cone surface and curved hemisphere surface are exposed. The cone slant height is sqrt(4^2+4^2) = 4sqrt(2), giving cone area pi x 4 x 4sqrt(2) = 16pi sqrt(2). The hemisphere contributes 2pi(4^2) = 32pi, so the total is 16pi(sqrt(2)+2) cm^2.
